h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תֵצֵא, ה׳ Ki Seitzei, 5
The Rebellious Son and the Repair of Israel’s Heart

p: "And you shall remove the evil," etc.
it is mentioned in the passage of the wayward and rebellious son,
and it is written in it (Devarim 21:21):
"And you shall remove the evil from your midst,
and all Yisrael shall hear and fear."
and in the Sifrei it is expounded:
"Wayward regarding the words of his father,
and rebellious regarding the words of his mother, etc."
to the voice of his father and the voice of his mother,"
"he does not listen to his father and mother,"
"to the voice of his father and mother";
not a single letter is superfluous.
"This son of ours is wayward and rebellious,
he does not listen to our voice"
And here is mentioned the expression
while at the beginning of the passage
there is no mention at all
And in the Sifrei it says:
Rather, he is judged on account of his end:
And in the end he will be put to
'And if there be in a man
Did he not steal from his father's house?
to steal from one's father's house?
also when at his end he will be
for all who are executed confess
וּמָצִינוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א ס, א)
and we find in the holy Zohar (Zohar I 60a):
'Hashem is a Man of war,' etc.;
one who is a great man and a tzaddik,
with David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
and fathered a wayward and rebellious son
to the voice of his father and the voice of his mother"
this is along the lines of
that is, the Sages of Yisrael,
And this is what it says:
"to the voice of his father and the voice of his mother":
voice is the life of speech
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רסא, א)
and that is: "the voice of his father"
the aspect of the Written Torah
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב ס, א)
we call it Torah she'b'al peh";
which are the life of speech.
And this is what it says, "wayward and rebellious,"
"Wayward regarding the words of his father,
and rebellious regarding the words of his mother;
wayward regarding the words of Torah,
and rebellious regarding the words of the prophets."
the aspect of the Written Torah
And "rebellious regarding the words of his mother"
regarding the words of the prophets;
is the attribute of Knesses Yisrael,
"and he does not listen to them";
even though the father is "a man,"
and his mother too is a righteous woman,
along the lines of what it says (Kiddushin 31b):
the sound of his mother's footsteps,
I will rise before the Shechinah, etc.";
and along the lines of what was mentioned:
"and 'his mother' is none other than Knesses Yisrael";
and it is in their power
to bring words of Torah into his heart,
and he does not listen to them.
to the elders of his city
and to the gate of his place"
words of Torah into his heart.
that is, they point with the finger,
that it is in their power
to bring into him words of Torah
and fear of Hashem from his mother's side.
And this is why it says "zeh, this":
that they instilled in him words of Torah,
he is wayward regarding the words of his father
and rebellious regarding the words of his mother.
And this is what it says:
"He does not listen to our voice;
he is a glutton and a drunkard"
הוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (מִשְׁלֵי כג, כ)
along the lines of what it says (Mishlei 23:20):
among gluttonous eaters of meat," etc.
to the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רעא, ב)
to the aspect of the Written Torah;
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ (בָּבָא קַמָּא עב, א)
and along the lines of what we find (Bava Kamma 72a):
that there is in words of Torah
that is, the Torah she'b'al peh
that is contained in the Written Torah
And as soon as they bring him
words of Torah into his heart,
the flavors of the Written Torah
And this is what it says afterward:
"And if there be in a man
a sin worthy of death," etc.
And it says in a holy book
the holy Arizal, of blessed memory, eulogized
Rabbi Moshe Cordovero, of blessed memory,
"And if there be in a man"
that the reason is lacking in him,
and you hang him on a tree"
that is, because of the sin
which is the counsel of the serpent.
According to this we need to understand
"His corpse shall not remain overnight on the tree"
so why is it called "his corpse"?
"you shall not leave him overnight on the tree."
But it is along the lines of
yet according to what is answered,
that the dead outside the Land
as the dead outside the Land;
for the dead of Eretz Yisrael
because they have not yet rectified
the root of the serpent's corruption,
"and you hang him on a tree,"
which is the counsel of the serpent,
that he has not yet rectified
therefore it still says of him:
And this is also the reason
that it expounds in the Gemara cited above:
this is written about stillborn infants";
for stillborn infants too were born
through the counsel of the serpent,
which is the sense of bodily pleasure,
and they have not yet rectified this blemish.
And although they did not sin in this world,
nevertheless the root of the blemish
of the counsel of the serpent
(Midrash Rabbah, beginning of Tazria, Vayikra Rabbah 14:5)
even the most pious of the pious, etc.";
to the passage of the wayward and rebellious son,
which in truth is an exception
to the rule of all those executed by the court,
and whose death is an atonement for them,
and they have a portion in the World to Come.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה
This is not so of the wayward and rebellious son:
they assist his father and mother
the holiness of the Written Torah
"And you shall remove the evil from your midst,"
that it will help to remove the evil
"And all Yisrael shall hear and fear"
and also a thought of teshuvah
the yetzer hara can still return
as long as one is in this world.
And this is what the Sifrei says:
that is, that already before his death
the light of the Written Torah
that is, if he became liable to death
like all those liable to death
although all who are executed confess
and have a portion in the World to Come,
and he enters the World to Come
his death is while he is guilty.
And this is what the Sifrei concludes:
and in the end he will be put to
'And if there be in a man
for all those liable to death
while this wayward and rebellious son,
of the Written and Oral Torah,
and he is in truth now innocent
and nevertheless they put him to death;
and this is an unusual death.
the root of the serpent's blemish.
"And if there be in a man
that it be lacking with him
the reason for the judgment of death,
why the innocent should be put to death;
"and you hang him on a tree"
the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil;
that is, in order to rectify
of the counsel of the serpent,
and to rectify in all Yisrael,
to bring fear into their hearts,
